description:
Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and wait for their answers.

Use it for a decision you genuinely cannot infer. Each question carries 2-4
concrete options; mark the one you recommend. The run pauses, and answers come
back in `answers` keyed by each question's `header`.

Prefer this over a prose question whenever the answer is a choice among known
options. For free-form input, ask in prose and end your turn. Only ask when it
changes what you do next — otherwise take the obvious default and proceed.

label.description: The choice shown to the user (1-5 words).

header.description: Few-word label, shown as a chip and used as the answer key.

multi_select.description: Allow selecting more than one option.

questions.description: Questions to ask at once. An 'Other' free-text choice is always added for the user, so do not add one yourself.

output_schema.description: Result of an ``ask_user`` call: the user's answers to the questions.

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

answers.description: The user's answers keyed by each question's header. Each value is the chosen option label(s) or the custom text they typed for 'Other'.

interaction_fallback.description: True when a remote harness runtime could not pause and the model must ask the question conversationally instead.

output_schema.title: AskUserResponse

description:
Get one operation's description and input/output schemas.

Call this before running an operation you have not run before -- the input
schema is what `run_connector_operation` validates `arguments` against.

Show a pod resource or a rendered view to the user.

Reach for this whenever the useful answer is more than short prose: several
values, records, statuses, comparisons, a timeline, or a chart render as a
WIDGET instead of being described. After creating or changing a pod resource,
display it rather than only saying it was created.

Set `type` and, for most types, a `name` — omit `name` to show all resources
of that type. FILE takes a pod `path`, so upload sandbox deliverables with
`lemma files upload` first and never pass a workspace path. WIDGET takes
exactly one of `content` or `public_url`; load the `lemma-widget` skill before
your first widget, and build an app instead when the UI needs React, routing,
or real state.

This tool only displays. Use `ask_user` for choices and `request_approval` for
permission.

field.description: Table column name to filter on.

type.description: Kind of resource the user should see.

name.description: Pod resource name; omit to show all of that type.

path.description: Pod file path, for FILE. Never a workspace path.

content.description: Inline SVG or HTML, for WIDGET. No DOCTYPE/<html>/<head>/<body>.

loading_messages.description: Messages shown while a WIDGET renders.

filters.description: Record filters {field, op, value}, for TABLE.

query.description: Read-only SQL for TABLE on RLS-disabled tables; prefer `filters`.

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

app.description: Displayed workspace app name when applicable.

url.description: Short-lived public URL for displayed workspace apps.

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the app access URL expires.

description:
Run a shell command in the private conversation workspace.

Use it for repo inspection, builds, tests, file edits, and `lemma` CLI calls
(pod credentials are pre-injected). `localhost` is this container, not the
Lemma backend.

Default (`tty=false`) returns after a short wait; a command still running
returns a `process_id` instead of blocking. `tty=true` starts a real terminal
for interactive commands. Either way, drive the process afterwards with
`manage_process` — poll or send input with `action="input"`, stop it with
`action="kill"`, and use `action="list"` to find processes started earlier.

cmd.description: Shell command to run, exactly as in a terminal.

comment.description: One-line statement of intent, shown to the user.

max_output_tokens.description: Truncate stdout/stderr past this many tokens.

tty.description: Allocate an interactive terminal. Required for commands that stay alive or wait for input (`npm run dev`, `python`). Such a process does not survive an idle pause.

cols.description: Terminal width for `tty` commands; widen for wide output.

workdir.description: Working directory; relative paths resolve inside the workspace.

yield_time_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for output before returning.

timeout_seconds.description: Block up to this many seconds instead of the default 30s yield window; always returns `completed: true` with no `process_id`.

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

stdout.description: Captured standard output from the command or interactive session.

stderr.description: Captured standard error from the command or interactive session.

exit_code.description: Process exit code when the command has completed.

completed.description: Whether the process has finished. Interactive TTY sessions usually return `false` until exited.

process_id.description: Process ID to reuse with `write_stdin` for follow-up interaction when this interactive process is still running.

description:
Run Python in the conversation's shared IPython kernel.

Use it for data analysis, transformations, and calculations that are awkward
in shell. Kernel state — imports, variables, objects — persists across calls,
so build up an analysis stepwise instead of repeating setup.

comment.description: One-line statement of intent, shown to the user.

code.description: Python code to execute in the shared task kernel. The final expression value is returned separately when available.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum execution time in seconds before timing out.

description: Return normalized final agent data for adapter-side handling.

output_schema.description: Structured final agent result returned by the output tool.
output_schema.title: FinalAgentResult

description:
Drive a running sub-agent you spawned.

action='send'  → post a follow-up message (starts a new turn); needs content.
action='await' → block until a run finishes (bounded by timeout_seconds); needs run_id.
action='stop'  → request a graceful stop.

input_schema.description: Drive a running sub-agent you spawned.

action.description: 'send' a follow-up message (starts a new turn), 'await' a run to finish, or 'stop' a running sub-agent.

content.description: Message to send. Required when action='send'.

run_id.description: Run id from spawn. Required when action='await'.

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to block when action='await' before returning a still-running handle. Keep this small and poll again with query_subagents(mode='messages') for long-running children rather than blocking the parent run.

input_schema.title: InteractSubagentRequest

description:

List the available skills. Pass `{}`; call before `load_skill`.

input_schema.description: Empty request model for listing workspace skills.

description.description: Short description of what the skill does.

path.description: Backing path to the skill's `SKILL.md` file. Pod skills use `/skills/...` paths.

workspace_path.description: Workspace-visible absolute path to the skill's `SKILL.md` file.

workspace_dir.description: Workspace-visible absolute path to the root directory for this skill.

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

description:
Transcribe a voice message or audio file to text.

`file_path` may be a pod path (e.g. `/me/telegram/voice.ogg`) or a workspace
path; common formats are supported directly.

The transcript is for YOUR understanding — act on it as if the user had typed

file_path.description: Path to the audio file to transcribe. Accepts a pod datastore path (e.g. /me/telegram/voice.ogg) or a workspace path.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language hint (e.g. 'en'). None = auto-detect.

description:
Load a skill's `SKILL.md`, or one resource file from inside it.

Omit `resource_path` to get `SKILL.md` plus the list of the skill's resource
files; pass a path from that list to read one.

name.description: Skill name to load, for example `skill-creator`.

resource_path.description: Optional relative path to a file inside the skill directory. Omit to load `SKILL.md` (the response also lists the skill's resource paths); pass a path from that list to load that resource instead. Must not be absolute.

workspace_path.description: Workspace-visible absolute path to the resource file.

description:
Drive a process started by `exec_command`.

`input` sends characters to a running process, or polls its output when
`chars=""`. `kill` stops it. `list` shows tracked processes in this
workspace. `resize` changes an interactive terminal's `cols`/`rows`. All but
`list` need `process_id`.

input_schema.description: Drive a process started by `exec_command` (interactive or long-running).

action.description: What to do with the process.

process_id.description: From `exec_command`. Required for every action but 'list'.

description:

``app`` (default) returns an in-app link for a signed-in member plus a
short-lived download url. ``public`` mints a signed link anyone can open —
it expires and dies after ``max_hits`` downloads.

description:
Read records from a pod table.

Pass ``record_id`` to fetch a single record; omit it to list records with

Reads across tables (joins, aggregates, subqueries) including RLS-enabled

Read a pod file as text, or a document as converted markdown.

Documents are converted and cached at upload, so reading is instant — never
download and re-parse one. Use ``pod_view_document_pages`` to see pages

You receive the page images inline; the transcript keeps only short-lived URLs.

description:
Write text content to a pod file, creating or overwriting it.

Without an absolute path, the file lands in your default pod working
directory (`/me/c/{date}/{slug}`) — a stable, private location scoped to
this conversation. Writes under your own `/me/...` (including that default
location) never need approval; writes to a shared pod path may.

path.description: Pod file path. A relative path resolves against `/me/c/{date}/{slug}` — write there unless a specific shared location is needed.

overwrite.description: If false, reject the write when the file exists.

description:
Create, update, or delete a record in a pod table (requires record.write grant).

- ``action="create"`` — needs ``data`` (column -> value).
- ``action="update"`` — needs ``record_id`` and ``data``.
- ``action="delete"`` — needs ``record_id``.

action.description: 'create' a new record, 'update' an existing one, or 'delete' one.

data.description: Column -> value mapping, e.g. {"title": "Q3 report", "amount": 42}, or a JSON-encoded string of it. Required and non-empty for 'create' and 'update'.

description:
Inspect the sub-agents you spawned.

mode='list'     → child conversations with latest run status (status='ACTIVE'
                  filters to running ones).
mode='messages' → latest messages from one child; needs conversation_id.

status.description: mode='list' filter: 'ACTIVE' for only running children.

after_sequence.description: mode='messages': only return messages after this sequence.

description:
Ask the user to approve an action you lack permission for, then run it.

Call this when a tool fails with a permission error (403) or the action needs
the user's authority — deleting data, sending email, a privileged command.
Describe the FULL action; do not rely on prior context. The run pauses for an
approval card, and on approval the backend executes the tool with the *user's*
authority and returns its result here. On denial nothing runs.

tool_name.description: Tool to run on approval, e.g. "exec_command". Must be one you have.

args.description: Complete arguments for that tool, e.g. {"cmd": "lemma records delete orders --id 42"}.

title.description: Short user-facing title for the approval card.

payload.description: Extra structured detail for rendering or audit.

permission_ids.description:
Copy `approval.permission_ids` verbatim from the failed tool
result. Lets "approve for session" cover these actions for the rest of the
conversation instead of re-prompting.

AgentRunApprovalDecision.description: User decision scope for a run approval.
AgentRunApprovalDecision.title: AgentRunApprovalDecision

Carries both the user's decision and, when approved, the result of running

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

decision.description: The user's decision: APPROVE_ONCE, APPROVE_FOR_SESSION, or DENY.

result.description: The wrapped tool's result when executed as the user.

description:
Run an operation on an installed connector.

`arguments` must match the operation's input schema -- fetch it with
`describe_connector_operation` first. A file result larger than the inline
limit is written to the pod datastore and returned as a reference; pass
`output_path` to choose where it lands.

account_id.description: Connected account to use; omit for the caller's own.

output_path.description: Pod path to save a file result to, e.g. /me/report.pdf.

description:
Speak a reply: synthesize audio and deliver it as a voice note.

Text is the default modality, so call this only when voice is genuinely
wanted. Delivery is automatic — a native voice note on chat surfaces, an
audio player on web.

The audio IS your reply. Do not call `display_resource` afterward, and do not
restate the same words as text; add a text line only if it says something
different.

output_file_path.description: Optional pod datastore path for the generated .mp3 (e.g. /me/speech/reply.mp3). Defaults to a generated /me/speech/<id>.mp3.

voice.description: Optional provider-specific voice/model id. None = default.

audio_file_path.description: Pod datastore path of the generated audio file.

description:
Find operations by what they do, ranked by relevance.

Start here rather than guessing an operation name: an install can expose
hundreds of operations, and the names are provider-specific. Leave
`auth_config` unset to search every installed connector at once -- each hit
names the `auth_config` to run it against, so you do not need to know which
install provides a capability before searching for it.

auth_config.description: Installed connector to search, by its auth-config name. Omit to search every connector installed in the organization -- prefer that when you know the task but not which install provides it.

query.description: Free text to rank operations by; omit to list.

description:
Suspend this turn and pick it up later, where you left off.

Use it when the work has a real gap — a build to check back on, something
that needs time to settle. You wake in the same conversation with the same
history.

Three things that bite:
- **Your sandbox does not survive.** `/workspace`, background processes, and
  your shell cwd are gone on wake. Write anything you need to the pod first.
- **Waking proves nothing happened.** `TIMER` means your time elapsed and
  nothing more — check the thing you were waiting for.
- **Every wake replays the whole conversation**, so one longer sleep beats a
  poll loop.

Don't use it to wait on a person — ask and end your turn; their reply starts
a fresh run.

reason.description: One line shown to the user while you sleep. Be specific: 'waiting for the nightly build' beats 'waiting'.

seconds.description: How long to sleep, chosen from what you are waiting for — an eight-minute build wants one ~500s check. Under 30s is rejected; over 24h is clamped.

note_to_self.description: Handed back verbatim on wake. What you intended to do next.

output_schema.description: What the agent sees when it wakes.

error.description: Human-readable error details when the tool fails.

message.description: Human-readable status or follow-up information for the tool call.

woke_because.description: TIMER: your time elapsed — this says nothing about whether what you were waiting for actually happened, so check. CANCELLED: the wait was ended early.

output_schema.title: SnoozeResponse

description:
Start a pod agent as a linked child conversation; returns a handle.

Omit agent_name to spawn another instance of yourself for a targeted subtask.
Non-blocking: returns {conversation_id, run_id, status}. Use interact_subagent
(action='await') to wait, or query_subagents (mode='messages') to poll.

agent_name.description: Name of a pod agent you may execute. Omit (or pass your own name) to spawn another instance of yourself for a targeted subtask.

input.description: Task for the sub-agent as its first message: a plain instruction string (most common), or a JSON object of structured inputs.

description:
Load an image file from the private workspace and return it as binary tool content.

Use this for screenshots, generated images, charts, or any other visual artifact
that the agent should inspect.

PATH HANDLING:
- This tool reads only from the private current conversation workspace directory.
- Always pass a relative path such as `images/output.png`.
- Do not pass absolute paths or paths outside the current workspace directory.

pod_file_path.description: Image in the pod datastore, e.g. `/me/photo.jpg`. Set this or `workspace_file_path`, not both.

workspace_file_path.description: Image in the workspace sandbox, e.g. `images/output.png` — for artifacts you just produced. Set this or `pod_file_path`, not both.

description:
Add or update task-list items from markdown checklist lines.

A single line is upserted by its text; multiple lines replace the current
list as one authoritative snapshot. Returns the full task list.

todos.description: Markdown checklist lines, e.g. '- [ ] Fetch the Q3 report'; '[x]' means done. Several lines replace the list; one line is matched by text and flips just that task.
